scope.summary: This standard establishes audit objectives, criteria and practices, and provides guidelines for establishing, planning, conducting and documenting observations of audit(s) on occupational health and safety systems at work place. It provides guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of health and safety programs, verifying the availability and implementation of elements of occupational health and safety systems and the system’s ability to achieve defined safety objectives.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Management Guidelines (Chemical Department / Occupational Safety and Health)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 14489 is an auditing methodology rather than a direct physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its auditing framework and checklist is legally binding under various State Factory Rules (e.g., Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu), making third-party external safety audits by DGFASLI-approved auditors mandatory for Major Accident Hazard (MAH) and other hazardous factories.

requirements.detail: Establishes audit criteria to evaluate the effectiveness of health and safety programs, verify the existence and implementation of safety elements, and assess the system's ability to achieve defined objectives.

Identifies the core OHSMS audit subjects, categorized as 8 major elements and 76 sub-elements, incorporating management commitment, safe behavior of workers, hazard identification, and risk assessment.

Prescribes an exhaustive list of 29 types of physical and statutory records that must be systematically examined by the audit team, including policy, training logs, SOPs, work permits, IH surveys, medical files, and minutes.
Provides a comprehensive sample safety audit checklist of detailed questions covering all elements, designed to guide field visits, interviews, and verification of compliance with OHS guidelines.
First Revision incorporates critical evaluation of behavioral safety, analyzing safe and unsafe acts, worker safety habits, and behavior-based training outcomes at the workplace.

Checklist specifically details detailed checks on chemical transfer pipelines, auditing underground/overground corrosion protection, booster pumps, public domain extensions, leak detectors, auto-shutoffs, and testing frequencies.

For the purpose of deciding conformance, any observed or calculated test result, noise level (dB), air concentration (ppm), or lux level during the audit must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant decimal places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14489 : 2018 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard code of practice for conducting occupational health and safety (OHS) audits at the workplace. Developed under the Chemical Department (CHD 08) and reaffirmed in 2023, this standard unifies safety inspection frameworks, risk assessment guidelines, and legal compliance checks. It outlines a structured methodology consisting of preliminary review, on-site audits, record examinations (29 records in Annex B), and field surveys (using the comprehensive checklist in Annex C). By structuring audits around 8 major elements and 76 sub-elements (Annex A)—including the modern addition of worker behavior-based safety—the standard ensures proactive hazard mitigation, occupational health protection, and regulatory compliance for chemical, MAH, and general manufacturing industries across India.
